items.topic: Testing LAN reachability of the review app from the host Mac
items.claim: Curling the Mac's own LAN IP shows the review app is reachable from other PCs.
items.fact: Traffic to the host's own IP never leaves the machine, so the check proves nothing. The review server (target/review-app/server.py) was changed so log_message prints every request from a non-127.0.0.1 client (time, IP, request line). If nothing is logged after a colleague tries, the network is dropping the traffic (Wi-Fi client isolation, a different subnet, or a stale IP). Operator's fix for 'other PCs can't load it': they were on the wrong network, so run 'check ip' (ifconfig plus route -n get default). The LAN IP changes with the network (172.28.1.16 became 192.168.10.219). The server binds 0.0.0.0, so only the address changes and no restart is needed. Tailscale (100.x) works regardless of the LAN.
items.evidence: session 2026-11-06T10:12-10:14, operator 'check ip! i was ont he wrong network'

items.fact: The review app shares one state file (openspec/changes/restructure-blueprints-for-kb/review-state.json). Decision and note saves send only the changed field and the server merges it into the file, so edits to different items are safe. Same note: last writer wins. New topics are saved as a whole object, so a stale browser copy can overwrite another person's edit to a topic's title, sentence or target. Other users' decisions and notes show only after a reload, and new topics refresh on tab focus. The agent offered polling every few seconds plus field-level topic saves. The operator did not answer, and went on to ask for the AI chat view.

items.topic: Add a shared AI chat view to the review app using the pi-dashboard
items.fact: Operator request: add an AI chat view to the review app that uses the operator's pi-dashboard. Provide this session so all users of the site can converse with it. Operator hints: 'You can use the dashbaord's plugin attachment to create the site', 'Dahsboard ahs a way to provide teh caht view in other application', and then 'Does not look good! use our caht view!'. The agent first built a relay: server.py reads the session transcript JSONL (PI_SESSION_FILE) and POSTs to /api/session/:id/prompt. Config file: openspec/changes/restructure-blueprints-for-kb/review-chat.json {sessionId}. Prompts arrive as '[Review site · <name> · topic: <topic>] msg'. Clients poll every 2s with the panel open, every 10s with it closed. The operator rejected this UI as 'Does not look good' and asked for the dashboard's own chat view.

items.topic: pi-dashboard REST API for driving a session from external apps
items.fact: Base http://localhost:8000 (port in ~/.pi/dashboard/config.json). POST /api/session/:id/prompt with body {text, images?}: 200 {success:true}, 400 missing text, 404 no session, 502 no bridge. GET /api/sessions?id=<id> returns id, status, model, sessionFile, uiUrl, cwd, source. A session's transcript is its JSONL at sessionFile (also $PI_SESSION_FILE; $PI_SESSION_ID is the id) and can be tailed. There is no REST transcript endpoint: GET /api/events/:sessionId/:seq fetches a single event and GET /api/events/stream is SSE for transitions. CLI: 'pi-dashboard api <GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE> </path> [--data json] [--port n]'. Skill file: Pi-Packages/pi-agent-dashboard/packages/extension/.pi/skills/pi-dashboard/SKILL.md.

items.topic: Embedding the dashboard chat view in another app
items.fact: There are two unrelated mechanisms. (1) URL embed mode: open uiUrl + '?embed=1', which hides the session list. It is sticky per tab in sessionStorage['pi-dash-embed'] until ?embed=0 (hook useEmbedMode). (2) A React subpath export: import { ChatView, useSessionState } from '@blackbelt-technology/pi-dashboard-web/chat-embed' (docs/embedding-chat-view.md, change add-embeddable-chat-view). ChatView requires state (SessionState) and toolContext (ToolContext) and is fed by the dashboard WebSocket protocol. The dashboard docs are in Pi-Packages/pi-agent-dashboard/docs, and this repo's kb does not index them.

items.topic: pi-dashboard: letting LAN devices use the dashboard (bind vs trust vs pairing)
items.fact: Two settings govern LAN reachability. bindHost (Server page, default 127.0.0.1, needs a restart) and trustedNetworks / auth.bypassHosts (Security page, live). A loopback bind voids trusted entries outside it silently. Trusting a CIDR gives every device in it full dashboard access. Alternative, 'LAN knock pairing': pairing.acceptLanRequests=true (default false, live, no restart; Settings > Security > Network access). The device opens http://<host>:8000/pair?request and chooses Request access. The operator types the 8-digit code in the dashboard dialog, picks a tier (observe/control/operate, default operate) and approves. Then POST /api/pair/poll returns a bearer, which is exchanged via POST /api/device-session for an httpOnly pi_dash_device cookie (SameSite=Strict, Path=/api/). Knock gates: host_not_admitted 403, knock_not_lan 403 (peer not private/on-link, or any forwarding header), knock_disabled 403, knock_rate_limited 429, knock_pending 409, knock_busy 503. Unpaired LAN clients get /api/health networkAccess.error=network_not_allowed. Passkey invites need HTTPS (docs/acme-dns01-certs.md). docs/architecture.md ~L69, L3675, L4575-4690; faq.md L724, L1024.

items.topic: Operator rejected trusting the whole LAN; wants request-access pairing
items.claim: The agent offered trustedNetworks 192.168.10.0/24, the operator chose it via ask_user, and the agent edited ~/.pi/dashboard/config.json (a backup was copied first).
items.fact: Operator correction: 'no have the request access'. Use the dashboard's LAN request-access pairing with per-device approval. Do not set trustedNetworks, since that exposes all sessions, spawn, terminals and files to the whole LAN. The agent had already written trustedNetworks=['192.168.10.0/24'] to ~/.pi/dashboard/config.json (backup config.json.bak-<epoch>) and should have reverted it. acceptLanRequests was already true in this config, and /pair?request returned 200 on the LAN IP.

items.topic: Review app embed mode only works on localhost
items.claim: The review app's 'Dashboard view' (iframe of uiUrl?embed=1) works for all site users.
items.fact: The iframe loads the dashboard at uiUrl (http://localhost:8000/...), which is wrong or unauthenticated for LAN visitors. The review app's index.html gates it with isLocal (hostname localhost/127.0.0.1/::1), and the toast says 'needs a dashboard sign-in'. The fix must use the dashboard on the LAN IP with a paired device cookie, and build uiUrl from the request host instead of localhost. The final state was unresolved at the end of the chunk.

items.topic: agent-browser daemon conflicts when parallel commands are issued
items.fact: Sending several browser_ide commands in parallel gave 'A daemon for session default started concurrently with different daemon configuration' and 'Daemon failed to start'. Send one command at a time, and use ?v=N cache-busters when reloading the app. A [hidden] attribute needs '[hidden]{display:none !important}' in the app CSS when other rules set display. The first-open chat scroll bug was fixed by treating the first render as nearBottom.

items.topic: kb guard and context-mode hooks nag during source greps
items.fact: After 3 consecutive source greps without kb_search, the hook prints '[kb] ... Run kb_search before the next source search'. kb_search over this repo does not index Pi-Packages/pi-agent-dashboard docs, so it returned irrelevant hits (judo-ng AGENTS.md matches on 'embed'/'chat'). For dashboard questions, grep that repo's docs directly. Raw curl output triggers a context-mode hook warning, so use 'curl -s -o /tmp/x.json URL' and read the file. kb_search was also 'cancelled — no results retrieved' once while the index refreshed.

items.topic: Review app is exposed to the LAN and has prompt access to the operator session
items.fact: Warning to document: anyone on the LAN who opens the review site can prompt the linked pi session, which has shell, file edit and subagent tools. Only share on a trusted network. Their messages land in the operator's own conversation, so use a dedicated spawned session by setting its id in review-chat.json. review-state.json also showed an unattributed decision ('Scope decisions needed' = reject at 11:15) made by someone else.
